column3: Custom identifiers throughout: all_access, supporter, theme_sakura, theme_neon, rewind_5, rewind_20. No $rc_ magic identifiers - those carry subscription-duration semantics we do not have. The SAME identifier string is reused in every offering so client code keys UI off package.identifier alone. NOTE: monetization_catalog.csv lists package_type $rc_lifetime for all_access; reconciled here to the custom identifier all_access - if the dashboard is ever switched to the Lifetime type, PaywallPresenter's package map must change in the same commit

column6: Device fetch returns ofr_themes; force a null placement in the dev menu and confirm the sheet degrades to rental-only and never renders a core paywall

column6: Device fetch returns ofr_core; supporter package filtered out by SupporterVisibilityRule; paywall_viewed logs placement=bonus_district trigger=map_tap

column3: Serves ofr_rewind. Renderer: custom bottom sheet, opened ONLY by the player tapping the rewind chip (attempt >= 2, progress >= 40%). Fallback: NO offering (explicitly not the current offering) - if the placement returns nothing the sheet shows free/owned/rewarded rows and simply omits the pack rows
column4: RC > Offerings > Placements > + New placement
column6: Device fetch returns ofr_rewind; null-placement dev toggle confirms the sheet still opens with free options and zero purchase rows; EditMode test asserts no fetch is even attempted when attempt==1

column2: D1-35 Placement fallback policy (written down once)
column3: post_level_5 / bonus_district / shop -> fall back to the current offering (ofr_core or cached). theme_preview / rewind_failure -> fall back to NOTHING. Rationale: a mis-resolved placement must never turn a cosmetic sheet or a failure sheet into a core-paywall interrupt
column4: RC > Placements > (per placement) > Fallback offering setting
column6: Dev menu "break placements" toggle runs all five surfaces; QA signs off that no surface upgrades itself into a bigger ask

column2: D1-36 Build the Paywalls v2 paywall for post_level_5
column3: Built on ofr_core with a SINGLE package slot bound to all_access. Layout top-to-bottom per monetization_spec 4.1: close X top-left >=48dp at full opacity from frame 1; Night Harbor hero image; H1 "One ticket. Every line."; sub-head "All Access is the complete Cat Metro - one purchase, yours forever."; 5 benefit rows (Night Harbor 10 levels / both premium themes / daily free rewind doubled to 2 / ad-free guaranteed forever / gold conductor badge); price row; primary CTA "Unlock All Access - {price}"; secondary text button "Keep playing free"; three disclosure lines (one-time not a subscription / every level outside Night Harbor is free and solvable / purchases restore on any device); footer trust line "Fair by design: no forced ads, no energy, no loot boxes." NO countdown, nothing preselected, no exit-intent counter-offer
column4: RC > Paywalls (v2 editor) attached to ofr_core
column6: Rendered on 3 device tiers (low/mid/high): all three disclosure lines visible without scrolling on a 720p 16:9 screen; close button tappable in frame 1; 20 consecutive opens per tier with zero crashes (regression watch for Android paywall issues #745/#736/#732)

column2: D1-37 Price rendering inside the paywall
column3: All price text comes from RevenueCat paywall variables bound to the store product - no literal currency strings anywhere in the template or the app binary. Same rule for the custom UGUI screens (StoreProduct price string only)
column4: RC > Paywalls editor > text variables; Unity string table (pw_* keys)
column6: CI regex gate fails the build if any pw_* or shop string contains a currency symbol or a digit-dot-digit pattern; manual check in a non-USD storefront (INR) shows a correctly formatted local price

column3: CustomPaywallScreen (the production renderer for the other four placements) also backs post_level_5. A crash marker is armed before the native RCUI call; 2 armed-marker process deaths OR in-process exceptions set PaywallV2Disabled=true permanently on that device
column4: Unity PaywallPresenter.cs + save state (not a dashboard setting)
column6: Dev toggle forces an RCUI throw -> custom paywall appears seamlessly and a purchase still completes; after 2 armed deaths, paywall_viewed logs paywall_variant=fallback forever on that device

column3: Enable and configure the RevenueCat Customer Center: support email support@catmetro.io, restore-purchases entry, refund guidance pointing at Google Play (we cannot issue Play refunds ourselves), and a "missing purchase? switch Google accounts" help path. Device-test alongside Paywalls v2; custom help screen is the fallback
column4: RC > Customer Center configuration
column6: Opens from Settings and from the shop footer on device; restore from inside Customer Center produces restore_started/restore_completed; P1 - may ship in the first post-launch update if the device test is unstable

column2: D1-40 Request RevenueCat Ads beta access
column3: Submit on Aug 1. RevenueCat Ads is a public-beta TRACKING layer over an existing ad SDK - it does not serve ads (verified 2026-07-31). The AdMob convenience module is not available for Unity, so integration is manual AdTracker calls
column4: RC dashboard > Ads > Request access
column6: Request submitted and dated in ops log; status re-checked every 3 days; hard gate at D10 (Aug 10) - if not granted, the Model A contingency in monetization_spec 2.4 arms and the Catvertising narrative leads with AdMob data + the "ads only when the player asks" design

column3: IAdTracker maps 1:1 to TrackAdLoaded / TrackAdDisplayed / TrackAdOpened / TrackAdRevenue / TrackAdFailedToLoad. AdContext = {placement, network, adUnitId} with placement in {rewind_failure, double_tickets, daily_gift_double, streak_saver, theme_rental}. Ad SDK: Google Mobile Ads Unity 11.3.0 (fallback AppLovin MAX 8.6.4). Calls are no-op-safe before beta access is granted
column4: Unity CatMetro.Integrations.RevenueCat adapter (no dashboard step beyond D1-40)
column5: D1-40, AdMob app + 5 rewarded ad units created Aug 1
column6: A device session with one rewarded view shows the five AdTracker events in the RC dashboard within the same day; with beta access absent the same session must produce zero exceptions and zero dropped rewards

column3: RC > Integrations > OneSignal: OneSignal App ID + REST API key (Growth plan, $19/mo, locked). RevenueCat then writes purchase tags into OneSignal, which is the precondition for the payer_status suppression in the lapse-ladder journey
column4: RC > Integrations > OneSignal
column6: Test purchase on a license tester produces RC purchase tags on the matching OneSignal user within ~1 minute; payer users then fail the lapse-ladder entry condition (verified by a manual journey dry-run)

column3: Client sets the RevenueCat subscriber attribute $onesignalUserId = OneSignal.User.onesignalId immediately after OneSignal init AND again on any onesignalId change (it can arrive late or change); if it is still null, retry once on the next foreground. This is the only identity link - Cat Metro has no accounts and never calls RC LogIn
column4: Unity: Purchases.SetAttributes after OneSignal init (CatMetro.Integrations.OneSignal -> IPurchases)
column6: RC customer page shows $onesignalUserId populated for a fresh install within one session; a fresh-install run where OneSignal init is deliberately delayed 30s still ends with the attribute set (retry path)

column3: Cloudflare Worker at https://rc-hooks.catmetro.io/v1/revenuecat (~50 LOC): append-only write to KV + daily email digest to sushantsrikrish@gmail.com. NEVER in the purchase path - the game does not know this endpoint exists and never blocks on it
column4: RC > Integrations > Webhooks > + New webhook
column6: RC's Send test event returns 200 and the KV log gains a row; Worker cold-start latency logged (must not matter - fire and forget)

column3: Subscribe to: INITIAL_PURCHASE, NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE (this is the one that matters - it is how rewind pack fulfillment is reconciled), CANCELLATION (one-time product refunds surface here), EXPIRATION, BILLING_ISSUE, TEST. No subscription-only events - we ship no subscriptions
column4: RC > Integrations > Webhooks > event types
column6: Buy cm_rewind_20 on a license tester -> a NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE row appears in KV with the same store transaction id whose hash is in the device ledger; refund cm_all_access -> a CANCELLATION row appears and entitlement_changed(revoked) fires on device

column3: Set the Authorization header to a shared secret (stored as a Wrangler secret). The Worker returns 401 for anything else and counts 401s; the endpoint does no work before the header check
column4: RC > Webhooks > Authorization header field; `wrangler secret put RC_WEBHOOK_AUTH`
column6: curl without the header returns 401 and writes nothing to KV; RC's test event with the header returns 200

column3: Nightly Worker cron: count NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE events per product against the device-reported purchase_completed(txn_id_hash) analytics rows for cm_rewind_5 / cm_rewind_20. Any mismatch emails a one-line alert with the hashed ids. This is an AUDIT trail for disputes, not a grant mechanism - the ledger grants, the webhook only watches
column4: Cloudflare Worker cron trigger (0 7 * * *)
column6: Force a mismatch in staging (drop one analytics row) and confirm the digest flags it; steady state during the commercial beta must show zero mismatches for 7 consecutive days before the D24 submit

column3: Add a Test Store app inside the same RC project (supported >=8.3.0). Wire its key behind CM_TEST_STORE. Purpose: exercise offerings/placements/paywall/purchase/restore flows before Play credentials propagate and before the closed track is live

column2: SEP-53 Arm PW01 (only if Pro plan confirmed)
column3: If Pro: create the RC Experiment on placement post_level_5 with control ofr_core (all_access = cm_all_access @ $6.99) vs experiment-only offering ofr_core_b (all_access = cm_all_access_499 @ $4.99), 50/50, server-side. Experiment-only offerings (ofr_core_b, ofr_core_t8, ofr_core_f, ofr_themes_b, ofr_rewind_b, ofr_shop_b - see paywall_experiments.csv) are deleted after their readout; the four launch offerings are the only permanent ones
